asm-001.check: Peer TTM period misalignment not noted in peer rationale
asm-001.closing_evidence: valuation_inputs.json rationales.peers now has a TTM period-alignment paragraph. It gives AMD's TTM end of 2026-09-26 and each peer's: INTC 2026-09-26 (aligned), NVDA 2026-07-26, AVGO 2026-08-02, MRVL 2026-08-01. It says the lag biases EV/Sales and the median upward, because NVDA and MRVL, both lagged, are the two middle values (median 16.27x = mean of MRVL 16.07x and NVDA 16.48x in numerical/recompute/peers.json). It says the multiple is not adjusted and that the relative leg should be read as generous. I checked the dates and the cited growth against snapshot/peers.json filtered to acceptance at or before the cutoff: NVDA quarterly Revenues $81.615bn (to 2026-04-26) then $96.221bn (to 2026-07-26); MRVL $2.4178bn then $2.7393bn; latest ends NVDA 2026-07-26, AVGO 2026-08-02, MRVL 2026-08-01, INTC 2026-09-26. All match.
asm-001.detail: The peer EV/Sales leg compares AMD TTM revenue ending 2026-09-26 with peer TTM revenue ending 2026-07-26 (NVDA), 2026-08-02 (AVGO) and 2026-08-01 (MRVL); only INTC ends 2026-09-26. valuation_inputs.json rationales.peers does not mention that the fiscal periods differ (calendar vs fiscal). For fast-growing peers, a TTM that lags by about two months modestly inflates EV/Sales and so the relative leg ($450.35/share). Under the policy bands this does not change the rating: the relative leg would have to rise sharply to move the blended target above -10%. However, the period mismatch should be stated.
asm-001.required_evidence: rationales.peers (or the note) states each peer's TTM end date versus AMD's 2026-09-26 TTM and says whether the lag biases the median multiple

asm-002.check: Per-share valuation ignores the customer penny warrants (up to 320M shares, about 19% of diluted shares) and the related contra-revenue
asm-002.closing_evidence: Repaired as required. (1) valuation_inputs.json adds rationales.customer_warrants, which quotes Q-12 (160M each at $0.01), Q-18 (combined up to 320M), Q-16 (none vested as of 2026-09-26) and Q-17 (contingently issuable, excluded from diluted EPS). All 18 narrative quotes appear verbatim in snapshot docs (checked programmatically). The rationale states that the code's 1,661M diluted share count (valuation.json diluted_shares) contains no warrant shares. It gives direction (down) and size, which I recomputed from round-003 numerical/recompute/valuation.json (identical to round 2 and to computed/): DCF 324.517bn/1,981M = $163.8; relative 450.345 x 1,661/1,981 = $377.6; blend 0.6/0.4 = $249.3 vs $297.36 (-16.2%); upside -48.5% vs -38.6%. The rating stays Underperform. It labels the result an upper bound and analyst arithmetic. (2) Contra-revenue: Q-15 ($4.5bn reduction of future revenue) is acknowledged in assumptions.json revenue_qoq, valuation_inputs revenue_growth and customer_warrants. FY2026Q4 GAAP guidance is judged net, with a label saying the release does not say so. Not cutting cash flow is justified as non-cash consideration whose cost is taken as dilution (avoids double counting); this is consistent with the ASC 606 policy at periodic.txt line 666. (3) Net cash: rationales.net_cash and note.md state that the $1.2bn liability (Q-14) is excluded because it is 'not settleable in cash' (Q-13) and is reclassified to APIC on exercisability (periodic.txt line 666). (4) note.md (rendered lines 40-42 and 53) has the net-cash sentence, the dilution bullet ('roughly one-sixth', upper bound, rating remains Underperform), the contra-revenue bullet and a dilution risk line. share_change_qoq rationale explicitly excludes the warrants and points to the sensitivity.
asm-002.detail: The 10-Q (periodic.txt, Note 14, line ~1425) says AMD issued warrants to two customers (Oct 2025, Feb 2026), 'each entitling the holder the right to purchase up to 160 million shares of the Company's common stock at an exercise price of $0.01 per share'. The risk factor (line ~2368) puts the combined total at up to 320 million shares. Line ~1439 says the weighted-average fair value is $178.58 per share 'as most market conditions had been met'. Line ~1441 reports a warrant liability of $1.2 billion and $4.5 billion of unrecognized grant-date fair value 'that would be recorded as a reduction of revenue'. valuation.json divides equity value by diluted_shares = 1,661M, which excludes all warrant shares (none have vested). share_change_qoq (+0.2%/qtr) is based only on the historical diluted-share trend. Neither valuation_inputs.json nor assumptions.json nor note.md mentions the warrants as potential dilution. Yet the DCF capitalises the Data Center/Helios ramp (Q-3, Q-4), and the purchase milestones that vest these warrants are tied to that same ramp. So the model takes the revenue but not the dilution attached to it. Illustrative full-dilution effect (my arithmetic from valuation.json, not a code output): DCF equity $324.5bn / 1,981M shares = about $164 versus $195.37; relative leg $748.0bn / 1,981M = about $378 versus $450.35; blended about $249 versus $297, a cut of roughly 16% in the target price. Under the policy bands the rating stays Underperform (upside about -48% instead of -38.6%), but a possible 16% swing in the target, undisclosed, is a material valuation omission. Separately, the $4.5bn of unrecognized warrant value will reduce reported revenue as qualifying revenue is recognised. Guidance probably already nets this out for FY2026Q4, but the rationale for later-year revenue/FCF does not mention it. The $1.2bn warrant liability (other long-term liabilities) is reasonably left out of net cash because it is equity-settled at $0.01, but that choice should be stated.
asm-002.required_evidence: valuation_inputs.json rationales (and a sentence in note.md's valuation section or risks) acknowledge the customer warrants (up to 320M shares at $0.01, quotable from periodic.txt) as potential dilution not reflected in the code's diluted share count. They state the direction and rough size of the effect on the per-share target (and confirm the rating would not change), or explain with evidence why the dilution is treated as immaterial or not probable. They also note that the unrecognized warrant value will reduce future reported revenue, and state why the warrant liability is excluded from net cash.

asm-003.check: Warrant-dilution sensitivity describes vesting as purchase-milestone driven only; the stock-price-target conditions are omitted
asm-003.detail: Still open. The candidate is unchanged since review-01: the sha256 values of assumptions.json, valuation_inputs.json, note.md and narrative.json match generator/manifest.json. snapshot/docs/periodic.txt line 1425 says the warrants vest in tranches 'as the customers reach specified purchase milestones and the Company's stock price meets specified targets, including, for certain tranches, stock price performance relative to a market index'. It also says each tranche becomes exercisable only after technical and commercial conditions are met. valuation_inputs.json rationales.customer_warrants still says only 'customer purchase milestones and other conditions'. The note.md Customer warrants bullet still says vesting 'depends on customer purchase milestones'. Neither mentions the share-price hurdles. Those hurdles matter when reading the 320M full-dilution ceiling, because the note's own thesis has the price falling towards a $297 target from the $483.90 close. Full dilution is still a valid upper bound, its direction is right and the rating is unaffected, so this stays minor.
asm-003.required_evidence: customer_warrants rationale (and optionally the note bullet) mentions that vesting also requires AMD share-price targets, and comments briefly on how this interacts with the full-dilution upper bound

prov-001.check: EPS run-rate judgment cites the discrete tax benefit but omits the offsetting $1.2bn noncash warrant charge
prov-001.closing_evidence: generator/note.md Results net-income bullet (rendered in numerical/recompute/note_rendered.md) now cites both one-off items by verbatim quote: [[Q-7]] (discrete tax benefit related to stock-based compensation of $772 million, periodic.txt lines 1481/1732) and [[Q-11]] (noncash charge of $1.2 billion from warrant-liability remeasurement within Other income (expense), net, periodic.txt line 1441). The claim that 'reported EPS overstates the recurring earnings run rate' has been removed. It is replaced by a labelled judgment that the two items move EPS in opposite directions and that their net effect cannot be determined from the filing. That judgment is consistent with the evidence: the 10-Q gives no after-tax effect for the warrant charge (the income-tax note at line 1481 and the warrant note at lines 1425-1441 give none). The amounts appear only inside verbatim quotes, and all quotes Q-1 to Q-11 match snapshot/docs text exactly.
prov-001.detail: The Results section says: 'Net income benefited from a large discrete tax benefit in the quarter, so the reported EPS overstates the recurring earnings run rate (our judgment, based on the income-tax note in the 10-Q).' The 10-Q does report a Q3 discrete tax benefit related to stock-based compensation of $772 million (income tax benefit of $555 million, ETR (29.6)%). The same filing also reports Other income (expense), net of $(902) million for the quarter. The filing says this was 'primarily driven by the change in fair value of warrant liability of $1.1 billion' and that the company 'recorded a noncash charge of $1.2 billion, primarily related to a loss from remeasurement of the warrant liability'. That pre-tax noncash charge is larger than the $772 million discrete tax benefit and pushes reported EPS the other way. The note uses only one of the two items, so the directional conclusion ('overstates the recurring earnings run rate') is not supported by the evidence it cites, and it may be wrong. The judgment label does not fix a one-sided reading of the filing.
prov-001.required_evidence: The note.md net-income bullet either names both one-off items (the $772M discrete tax benefit and the roughly $1.1-1.2bn noncash warrant remeasurement charge in other income) and draws a conclusion consistent with both, or drops the claim that reported EPS overstates the run rate. Any amounts cited must be available as {{key}} values or as quotes.

prov-002.check: Contingently-issuable treatment of warrant shares is paraphrased without citing its quote
prov-002.detail: Not repaired (the candidate is unchanged since review-01: note.md sha256 63cbcfd6... matches manifest.json). In Model and valuation, the customer-warrants bullet still reads 'The 10-Q treats the warrant shares as contingently issuable and excludes them from diluted EPS until they vest' with no [[Q-17]] marker. The [[Q-*]] markers used in note.md are Q-1 to Q-7, Q-11, Q-12, Q-13, Q-15 and Q-16; Q-17 is not among them. The statement is accurate: Q-17 in narrative.json matches periodic.txt word for word ('...excluded from the computation of basic and diluted earnings per share until all the conditions for the warrants to become vested and exercisable have been satisfied'). Shortening this to 'until they vest' does not materially change the meaning, but the claim cannot be traced the way the neighbouring Q-12, Q-13, Q-15 and Q-16 claims can.
prov-002.required_evidence: note.md cites [[Q-17]] where it states the contingently issuable / EPS-exclusion treatment
